references.text: The Passover shall be a memorial day, celebrated as a festival to the Lord throughout your generations, an everlasting ordinance.
On this same day the Lord brought the Israelites out of Egypt, organized by their divisions.
Moses reminds the people to remember this day when they came out of Egypt, from the house of slavery, and how the Lord brought them out with a mighty hand.
The commandment to keep the month of Passover and celebrate the Passover for the Lord, because the Lord brought them out of Egypt by night.
The Passover lamb shall be slaughtered in the evening at sunset, at the time when they came out of Egypt.
The Lord who watches over Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps; he is a guardian who keeps watch.
Moses announces that the Lord will go out through the midst of Egypt at midnight, on the night when the exodus took place.
At midnight the Lord struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, that same night when the Lord kept watch over Israel.
The prophecy that the Lord will go before them and be their rear guard for Israel, a reference to the Lord's protective watch.
The verses complement each other by showing that the deliverance of Israel during the night was simultaneously God's judgment on Egypt.
Uses the exodus from Egypt as a theological basis for God's ownership of the people.
A New Testament allusion confirming the exodus from Egypt as an act of God's salvation.
Connects the 'watchnight' to the concept of an eternal memorial and sign of God's deliverance.
Highlights that the exodus from Egypt was intended to make the people know God's presence.
A direct narrative link where the prophets explain the meaning of the ongoing 'watchnight'.
The forerunner (prophecy) in 6:7 is fulfilled in the event described in 12:42.
